propositions: Bridge git delivery is abandoned after a single transport failure (TLS/DNS/timeout), leaving unpushed commits that are silently lost and detected only by heartbeat canary

The push.py retry logic retries only genuine non-fast-forward errors but treats all other non-zero push outcomes as terminal on first attempt, conflating permanent policy violations with transient transport faults
Transport errors including TLS certificate verification, DNS resolution, connection timeouts, and git command timeouts receive zero retries despite being transient and recoverable
Both the explicit fetch recovery leg and the promisor on-demand fetch inside git merge lack transport retry logic, with merge recovery producing separate terminal reason 'merge-recovery-blocked'
A bounded retry strategy with 3 total transport attempts per leg and injected backoff (0.5s, 2.0s) is needed, while genuine merge conflicts and policy declines must remain terminal on first attempt
